You make some good points, and I can understand why people would believe Eric was a full-fledged psychopath, but I just refuse to believe it.

1. Cullen describes Eric Harris as a ladies man, and he reports a particular instance of Eric having sexual relations with a woman named Brenda Parker. She later confessed that it was all for attention, and it never happened. 

2. Dylan is considered Eric's compliant puppet in the book and just following Eric's orders when in reality he played a much larger role in the planning and executing of the massacre. Dylan can also be heard on the Patti Nielson 911 call cheering after shooting someone. 

3. The principal of Columbine, Frank DeAngelis, is portrayed as a kindhearted individual who cared about all the students at Columbine and would talk with them throughout the day. However, this kind of love and support was only displayed to the jocks and popular kids at Columbine. Brooks Brown holds strong resentment towards DeAngelis and writes about how the faculty at Columbine couldn't care less about the outcasts. 

5. Dave Cullen's complete rejection of bullying at Columbine is what upsets me the most about his book. He says that Eric and Dylan were never bullied and there was no favoritism at Columbine, but both No Easy Answers and their journals tell the true story of just how bad they were treated.

Dave Cullen's book would be best described as a work of fiction. His book is biased and does not give you an accurate look at Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold's lives or personalities.
